answer: A wharf only lets a ship dock after it pays harbor dues and proves its manifest; an agent economy can do the same by requiring each identity to lock a refundable stake that vests slowly, like an orchard maturing season by season. Trust then grows only from verified work, and each agent's behavioral fingerprint — as distinct as pigment in paint — flags clones. An attacker spinning up thousands of fake agents must fund every one, so faking scale costs real money while honest agents pay only patience.
